title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance, and Manager Guide 2026
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Overview

This document describes Redwood Inference's canonical people operations processes for hiring, onboarding, performance reviews, feedback cycles, manager responsibilities, and related templates. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering leaders. Follow these processes to ensure a consistent candidate and employee experience, fair assessment, and timely execution across teams.

Key goals
- Time-to-offer target: 30 calendar days from req approval to signed offer for most roles.
- Candidate experience NPS target: > 70.
- New hire activation: 90% of new engineers have first PR or customer-facing task within 30 days.
- Performance calibration: Zero unexplained rating variance across teams in calibration cycles.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Intro: The hiring process balances speed, candidate experience, and rigorous evaluation. People-ops owns the process and tooling; hiring managers own role definition, sourcing plan, and decision.

1.1 Requisition & role definition- Owner: hiring manager- Steps:
  1. Draft a job brief in Lever using the company template (role, top competencies, success metrics for 6 months, salary band).
  2. Get budget and headcount approval from finance (email thread or Workday approval).
  3. Submit the req in Lever and notify your people-ops recruiter.
- Good practice: Include 3 measurable objectives for the first 90 days and 2-2 must-have technical skills.

1.2 Sourcing and screening- Owner: recruiter + hiring manager- Screening SLA: initial phone screen within 5 business days of receiving candidate application.
- Steps:
  - Recruiter validates basic fit (location, right-to-work, salary band) and schedules initial phone screen.
  - Use the standardized phone-screen scorecard (competencies: communication, role fit, fundamentals).

1.3 Interview loop design- Owner: hiring manager- Minimum stages for engineering roles:
  - Recruiter phone screen (30 min)
  - Technical screen (45-60 min): algorithmic or system design as applicable using internal exercise bank.
  - Onsite / virtual loop (3-4 interviews, 50 min each): 
    * Coding (pair-programming or take-home review)
    * System design or architecture
    * Team fit / collaboration / cross-functional
    * Manager interview (expectations, growth plan)
- Use timeboxed exercises and the official scorecards. For senior roles add a leadership interview and cross-team stakeholder interview.

1.4 Decision & offer- Owner: hiring manager + recruiter + people-ops- Steps:
  1. Collect interview scorecards within 24 hours of final interview.
  2. Hiring manager writes a short decision rationale (1-2 paragraphs) referencing scorecards and recommended level and comp.
  3. People-ops validates band and recommends competitor market adjustment if needed.
  4. Recruiter extends verbal offer and follows with written offer within 48 hours.
- Targets: 80% of offers accepted within 7 days of offer.

1.5 Background checks & compliance- Owner: people-ops- Redwood runs a standard background check for all hires in jurisdictions where permitted. For regulated hires or private deployments teams, add role-based screening (credit/DBS) as required.

1.6 Disqualified candidate handling
- Respectful closure: provide concise, constructive feedback within 7 days of decision when requested. Always follow non-discriminatory guidelines.

2) Onboarding (first 90 days)

Overview: Onboarding at Redwood is structured into pre-boarding, week 1, month 2-3. The goal is to ramp new hires quickly while building relationships and psychological safety.

2.1 Pre-boarding checklist (before day 1)- Owner: recruiter + IT + manager
- Offer signed and HR packet complete- Equipment order placed (laptop, monitors, peripherals) and shipped with tracking- Provisioning request to IT (account creation, Slack, email, VPN, repo access request)- Manager assigns a buddy and schedules day 1 1:1

2.2 Day 1 / Week 1- Owner: manager
- Company orientation (people-ops-led)  - benefits, code of conduct, security briefing- Team orientation: team mission, org chart, current projects, communication norms- Access checklist: verify access to CI, repo, issue tracker, and internal docs- 30-min meet-and-greet schedule with immediate collaborators

2.3 First 30 days- Goals:
  - Complete assigned onboarding learning path (internal docs, security training, product overview).  - Ship first small-ticket task (bugfix or documentation PR) and seek feedback.
- Manager actions:
  - Weekly 1:1 with documented objectives and blockers  - Weekly onboarding sync with people-ops for feedback on process

2.4 30-90 days (growth and exposure)- Goals:
  - Complete 30-60-90 plan with measurable milestones (owned feature, demo to team).  - Participate in one cross-functional project or customer-facing interaction.
- Manager actions:
  - Biweekly career conversation and progress against goals  - Formal 90-day check-in (people-ops template) to confirm role fit and next steps

Onboarding templates (available in Confluence)- 30-60-90 plan template- Manager onboarding checklist- Buddy checklist

3) Performance and feedback cycles

3.1 Performance cadence- Frequency: Formal performance reviews occur twice per year (mid-year and year-end) for all employees. Managers should also conduct informal check-ins quarterly.- Deliverables:
  - Self-assessment using the official template (1-2 pages) due 2 weeks before each review window.  - Manager assessment and proposed rating due 1 week before calibration.

3.2 Rating scale and criteria- Redwood uses a four-point scale: 1 = Needs improvement, 2 = Meets expectations, 3 = Exceeds expectations, 4 = Exceptional.- Criteria include: impact, execution quality, collaboration, ownership, and role-specific competencies. Calibrations normalize for role seniority and scope.

3.3 Feedback best practices- Encourage continuous feedback (peer-to-peer and manager-to-direct reports). Use the following pattern: Situation, Behavior, Impact, Next steps.- Document feedback in 1:1 notes and follow up with concrete actions.

3.4 Calibration and promotion cycles- Calibration panels (org-level) are scheduled after manager assessments. Panel composition: cross-functional managers and people-ops partner.- Promotion packets: manager submits: current role description, evidence of impact, peer feedback, and updated career profile. People-ops verifies comp band availability before promotion committee.

3.5 Performance improvement plans (PIP)- Use when a consistent rating of Needs improvement persists after coaching (typically 2+ months). PIP is a timeboxed (60-90 day) plan with clear success metrics and weekly check-ins. People-ops must review and sign off before issuance.

4) Manager responsibilities and manager guide

Overview: Managers at Redwood are responsible for recruiting, onboarding, performance management, career growth, and team health.

4.1 Hiring manager responsibilities- Define role and success metrics- Build diverse candidate slate and commit to interviewing panels with at least one diverse interviewer- Complete scorecards within 24 hours- Make timely decisions and document rationale

4.2 Onboarding & ramping- Provide a clear 30-60-90 plan and ownership of early deliverables- Assign a buddy, schedule recurring 1:1s, and set clear expectations for communication norms

4.3 Ongoing development- Conduct career conversations at least twice per year- Support learning budgets and provide stretch opportunities- Advocate for direct reports during calibration and promotion cycles

4.4 Psychological safety & inclusion- Hold regular team retros and ensure everyone has voice in planning and designs- Address microaggressions and bias promptly; escalate to people-ops for support

5) Templates, checklists, and links (summary)

Available templates (Confluence):
- Job brief template
- Interview scorecards (phone screen, coding, system design, manager fit)
- Offer approval checklist
- New hire 90-day check-in form
- Performance self-assessment and manager assessment templates
- Promotion packet template

6) Escalations and exceptions

- For urgent hiring needs (<14 day target) coordinate with head of recruiting to prioritize requisition.
- For compensation exceptions outside band, manager submits a business case to finance and people-ops; approval may take up to 5 business days.
- For legal or compliance concerns (visa, export controls, regulated customers), escalate to security-and-compliance and legal immediately.

7) Metrics and reporting

People-ops tracks these KPIs monthly:
- Time-to-fill (median days)
- Offer acceptance rate
- New-hire 90-day retention- Diversity of slate and hires by role- Hiring funnel conversion rates

8) FAQs

Q: What if a candidate asks for feedback after rejection?
A: Provide brief, factual feedback focusing on areas for development. Avoid comparative comments or subjective labels.

Q: How to handle international hires and visa sponsorship?
A: Engage legal and people-ops early; clear timelines are typically longer (60-120 days). Budget for immigration support costs.

Q: Where do I find templates and scorecards?
A: All templates are in Confluence under /confluence/company-handbook/people-ops/templates.
